name: Dural Sinus Malformation Without Arteriovenous Shunt

criteria.description: Presence of an abnormally dilated dural venous sinus without evidence of arteriovenous shunting on imaging
No arteriovenous shunting demonstrated on cerebral angiography or MR angiography
Neurological symptoms consistent with venous hypertension or mass effect such as seizures or developmental delay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of dural sinus dilation without arteriovenous shunting confirmed by imaging plus at least one neurological symptom
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging to exclude arteriovenous shunts.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive macrocephaly due to venous sinus dilation
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic enlargement of the head in infants
searchTerms: progressive big head due to venous dilation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Venous sinus dilation visible on MRI without arterial feeders
searchTerms: dilated brain veins without artery involvement
seizures from high brain vein pressure
epileptic episodes due to venous hypertension
brain seizures related to vein problems

common.symptomName: Headache related to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: pain due to increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Papilledema due to raised intracranial pressure

occasional.symptomName: Irritability or inconsolable crying in infants
Focal neurological deficits such as hemiparesis

searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain needing shunting

rare.symptomName: Intracranial hemorrhage due to venous hypertension
searchTerms: brain bleeding from high vein pressure
brain hemorrhage due to vein issues

rare.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies secondary to mass effect
searchTerms: facial nerve palsy due to tumor

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory biomarkers
imaging: MRI showing dilated dural venous sinus without arterial feeders
MR angiography or cerebral angiography confirming absence of arteriovenous shunting
Possible signs of venous hypertension such as brain edema
genetic: No known genetic mutations currently associated
other: Clinical signs of increased intracranial pressure
Neurological examination revealing developmental delay or focal deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of arteriovenous shunting on angiography
High-flow vascular malformation with arterial feeders
Midline arteriovenous malformation involving the vein of Galen
Typically presents with high-output cardiac failure in neonates

redFlags: Rapidly increasing head circumference in infancy
Signs of raised intracranial pressure such as persistent vomiting or papilledema
New onset focal neurological deficits or seizures
references: Orphanet: Dural Sinus Malformation Without Arteriovenous Shunt (ORPHA:717564)
